extraction.diagnosis: Transient ischemic attack (TIA, a "mini-stroke") caused by new atrial fibrillation
extraction.hospital_summary: You had 20 minutes of right arm weakness and trouble speaking that went away fully. Your brain MRI showed no permanent damage. We started a blood thinner to prevent a stroke.

explanation.summary: You went to the hospital because you had a mini-stroke, called a TIA. This happened because of a new irregular heartbeat called atrial fibrillation. For 20 minutes, your right arm was weak and you had trouble speaking, but it fully went away, and your brain scan showed no lasting damage. The doctors started you on a blood thinner to help prevent a future stroke.

m1.how_to_take: Take 1 tablet by mouth two times a day, at 8:00 AM and 8:00 PM.
tips: Do not skip doses or stop taking this medicine unless your doctor tells you to.

m2.how_to_take: Take 1 tablet by mouth two times a day, at 8:00 AM and 8:00 PM.

m3.how_to_take: Take 1 tablet by mouth once a day at bedtime (9:00 PM).
tips: Your dose was increased from 20 mg to 80 mg.

m4.how_to_take: Take 1 tablet by mouth two times a day, with breakfast at 8:00 AM and with dinner at 6:00 PM.
tips: Your dose was lowered from 1,000 mg because of your kidney function.

m5.how_to_take: Take 1 tablet by mouth once a day at 8:00 AM.

m6.how_to_take: Take 1 to 2 tablets by mouth only if you need it, for headache or pain. You can take it again after 6 hours, up to 4 times a day.
tips: Do not take more than 3,000 mg in one day.

m7.how_to_take: Stop taking this medicine. Do not take aspirin anymore.
tips: You are now taking apixaban. Taking both aspirin and apixaban raises your risk of bleeding.

m8.how_to_take: Stop taking this supplement. Do not take ginkgo biloba anymore.
tips: Ginkgo biloba can increase bleeding when taken with apixaban.

signs: Your face is drooping on one side
You have weakness in your arm or leg
You have trouble speaking or understanding others
You suddenly cannot see well
You suddenly lose your balance
You have a sudden, very bad headache
You are vomiting blood, or your stool is black and tarry
A nosebleed or bleeding gums do not stop after 10 minutes
Your urine turns pink or red
You have bruises you cannot explain
Your pulse on the home monitor is below 50 or above 120

i1.text: Check your blood pressure and pulse every morning with your home monitor, and write down the numbers.

i2.text: Bring your log with you to your doctor visits.

i3.text: Do not drive until your neurologist says it is okay.

i4.text: Eat a low-salt diet that is also good for someone with diabetes.

i5.text: Take a walk every day, as much as you are able.

a1.text: You have a blood test to check your kidney function on October 28, 2026. You can go any time between 7:00 AM and 5:00 PM at Maplewood Outpatient Lab.

a2.text: You have a visit with Dr. Rachel Kim at the Neurology clinic on November 4, 2026 at 9:00 AM. It is at Maplewood Neuroscience Center, 4th floor.

a3.text: You have a visit with Dr. Samuel Osei at the Cardiology clinic on November 10, 2026 at 2:15 PM. It is at the Heart and Vascular Center, 2nd floor. Bring your blood pressure log with you.

a4.text: You will get a 14-day heart monitor. The clinic will call you to set this up.

a5.text: Call your primary care doctor within 1 week to make an appointment. The phone number is (203) 555-0130.
